newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to help small depositors in troubled banks.
newsitem.headline: Romania to help small depositors in troubled banks.

text.p: Romania's upper house of Senate on Tuesday passed a bill that empowered the country's central bank to give credits to two troubled private banks in a bid to help them redeem small depositors.
"The draft has been approved," a Senate official said.
To become effective, the bill must also be endorsed by the lower Chamber of Deputies.
In July, the central bank cut lifelines to Dacia Felix SA and Renasterea Creditului Romanesc Credit Bank SA on grounds the two banks had stopped payments for more than one month.
The central bank's move came after a year of continuous financial support to the two banks to keep them afloat.

Transylvania-based Dacia Felix came under central bank scrutiny last November with reports of bad loans of $200 million and a 1995 loss of 642.2 billion lei. Credit Bank was shaken by a management crisis after its president was arrested on fraud charges in January 1995.
The central bank has lodged its files on Dacia and Credit Bank with courts in Bucharest and the city of Cluj, which are expected to decide on the two bank's fate -- to liquidate or reorganise them.

Under the bill approved by the Senate on Tuesday, the central bank will give Dacia Felix and Credit Bank loans to cover payments for individuals' deposits and interests amounting to the equivalent of up to 10 million lei.
The two banks will transfer those funds to Casa de Economii si Consemnatiuni savings bank from where depositors can withdraw them, the bill said.
In August, the government approved an insurance deposit system for small depositors in banks. But the new mandatory- scheme would not apply retrospectively to cover Dacia and Credit Bank investors.
In September Dacia Felix started to pay individuals' deposits up to one million lei, unlocking some 235,000 accounts. ($=3,261 lei) -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
